# Hand-Crafted Template Counts in the Reported Question Generation System

## Introduction

The query asks how many hand-crafted templates were required in the work described by the supplied source. The source, document_2.txt, reports two distinct evaluations: a Freebase evaluation and an in-house power tool domain knowledge base evaluation. In both cases, the only human labor reported is question template construction, and each template is associated with a predicate in the knowledge base ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Consequently, the answer to the query is not a single undifferentiated number; it depends on whether one is referring to the Freebase evaluation, the power tool evaluation, or the combined reported total across both evaluations. The Freebase evaluation reports 106 hand-crafted templates, while the power tool evaluation reports 163 hand-crafted templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The combined reported total across the two evaluations is 269 templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Query Interpretation and Scope

The wording “How many hand-crafted templates did they have to make?” can be read in at least three ways. First, it may ask for the number used in the Freebase evaluation. Second, it may ask for the number used in the in-house power tool domain evaluation. Third, it may ask for the total number of hand-crafted templates across all reported evaluations. The source material supports all three readings because it explicitly reports two separate template counts and describes them as the reported template-construction figures for the system ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). A precise response therefore should state the counts separately and then provide the aggregate if a total is requested. This approach avoids conflating two different knowledge bases, two different predicate sets, and two different evaluation contexts ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Reported Template Counts

### Freebase Evaluation

In the Freebase evaluation, the work used 500 randomly selected triples ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). For those 500 triples, the paper reports 106 hand-crafted templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The triples shared only 53 distinct predicates, which means the authors made an average of 2 templates per predicate ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This average can be verified by dividing the reported template count by the reported predicate count: 106 ÷ 53 = 2 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Applying the templates to the triples generated 991 seed questions ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The experiment also retrieved 1,529 more questions from Google ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The design ties template creation to predicates, keeping the template set compact relative to the triple set ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Thus, for the Freebase component alone, the number of hand-crafted templates is 106 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

### In-House Power Tool Domain Evaluation

For the in-house power tool domain knowledge base, the paper reports 67 predicates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). For those 67 predicates, the authors hand-craft 163 templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This count differs from the Freebase template count because the domain-specific knowledge base has its own predicate set and required its own template set ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The average number of templates per predicate in this evaluation is approximately 2.43, calculated as 163 ÷ 67 ≈ 2.43 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The source does not report the number of triples or seed questions for the power tool domain in the supplied information, but it does report the predicate count and the hand-crafted template count ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Therefore, for the power tool component alone, the number of hand-crafted templates is 163 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

### Summary Table of Reported Figures

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Combined reported total | Two separate KBs | 120 (sum of separate sets) | 500 (Freebase only) | 269 | — | 991 (Freebase only) | 1,529 (Freebase only) |

Note: The combined total of 269 is an aggregation of the two separate hand-crafted template counts reported in the source ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The predicate sum of 120 is also an aggregation across two separate knowledge bases and should not be interpreted as a single unified predicate set ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The power tool evaluation’s triple count and question counts are not provided in the supplied information ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Relationship Between Predicates and Template Creation

The system’s design makes template creation follow the predicates present in the knowledge base ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Each template is associated with a predicate, and the paper states that the only human labor in this work is question template construction ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This predicate-centric approach means that the manual burden scales with predicate coverage rather than with the raw number of triples ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). In the Freebase evaluation, 500 triples reduced to 53 distinct predicates, and those 53 predicates required 106 templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). In the power tool evaluation, 67 predicates required 163 templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The difference in template counts is therefore explained by the different predicate sets and the different domain requirements, not by a single fixed template-to-predicate ratio ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

The Freebase evaluation achieved exactly 2 templates per predicate on average ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The power tool evaluation required about 2.43 templates per predicate ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This suggests that the power tool domain needed somewhat more question forms per predicate, possibly because of domain-specific relations or question types, although the supplied information does not elaborate on the reason for the difference ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). What is clear is that the authors did not create templates for every triple individually; instead, they created templates at the predicate level, which kept the template set compact relative to the triple set in the Freebase case ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Total Manual Template Count Across Evaluations

If the query is intended to ask for the total number of hand-crafted templates across both reported evaluations, the answer is 269 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This figure is obtained by adding the Freebase template count of 106 to the power tool template count of 163: 106 + 163 = 269 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The source describes these two counts as the reported template-construction figures for the system and states that they show the manual template-building effort scales with predicate coverage in each evaluation ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). However, it is important to note that these are two separate template sets for two different knowledge bases ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). They are not reported as a single unified template library. Therefore, the combined total of 269 is an aggregate of reported figures, not necessarily a count of templates that were all used simultaneously in one evaluation ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Implications for Manual Effort and System Design

The reported counts indicate that the manual effort in this system is concentrated on template construction rather than on annotating every triple ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). In the Freebase evaluation, 500 triples were covered by 106 templates, and those templates generated 991 seed questions ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The experiment then retrieved 1,529 additional questions from Google ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This combination of hand-crafted templates and retrieved questions suggests a hybrid strategy for building a question set, with templates providing a controlled seed set and external retrieval expanding coverage ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The predicate-linked design helps keep the manual template set compact relative to the triple set ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

For the power tool domain, the authors hand-crafted 163 templates for 67 predicates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This higher absolute number of templates than the Freebase evaluation may reflect the different predicate set and domain-specific requirements ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Even so, the effort remains predicate-driven rather than triple-driven ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The source states that the Freebase and power tool counts provide the reported template-construction figures for the system and that these figures show the manual template-building effort scales with predicate coverage in each evaluation ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). This is a significant design point because it means the human labor is bounded by the number of predicates, not by the number of triples or questions ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Limitations and Clarifications

Several clarifications are necessary to answer the query precisely. First, the source does not report a single grand total of hand-crafted templates for all evaluations in one sentence; the total of 269 is derived by adding the two reported counts ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Second, the Freebase and power tool template sets are for different knowledge bases and different predicate sets, so they should not be treated as one homogeneous set ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Third, the number of triples, seed questions, and retrieved questions for the power tool domain is not provided in the supplied information, so no comparable question-generation figures can be reported for that domain ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Fourth, the source states that the only human labor in this work is question template construction, which means the reported template counts are the primary measure of manual effort ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Finally, the average templates per predicate for the power tool domain is a derived value, not an explicitly stated figure in the source, and is calculated as 163 ÷ 67 ≈ 2.43 ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).

## Conclusion

The direct answer to the query depends on scope. For the Freebase evaluation, the authors had to make 106 hand-crafted templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). For the in-house power tool domain evaluation, they had to make 163 hand-crafted templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). If the question asks for the combined reported total across both evaluations, the number is 269 hand-crafted templates ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). The design ties template creation to predicates, keeping the template set compact relative to the triple set in the Freebase case, and the manual effort scales with predicate coverage rather than with the number of triples ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)). Therefore, the most complete and accurate response is: 106 templates for Freebase, 163 templates for the power tool domain, and 269 templates in total across the two reported evaluations ([Document_2, n.d.](document_2.txt)).
